   • borough (string)  
   • crime_rate_value (float, rate per 10 000 residents for Jan-Jun 2018)

2. Build a Python dict (or Series of lists) giving, for every borough, the list of its geographic neighbours from the supplied neighbour list.

3. Handle the single missing value:  
   • Drop the borough whose crime_rate_value is NaN from the working copy of the DataFrame.  
   • Remove that same borough from every neighbour list so that it never contributes to any combined local-area total.  
   • Because the borough itself has no value, it will not be evaluated as a candidate hot/cold spot.

4. For each remaining borough i:  
   a. Assemble the set Lᵢ consisting of borough i plus all of its neighbours that still have non-missing data.  
   b. Compute the local-area statistic Sᵢ = Σ_{j∈Lᵢ} crime_rate_valueⱼ (plain sum of rates).  
      – This directly addresses the question’s wording: “considering each borough TOGETHER WITH its neighbours as one combined local area.”

5. Form the vector S = [Sᵢ] for all boroughs retained in step 3.  
   • Let µ = mean(S) and σ = standard deviation(S) computed with ddof = 1 (sample SD).

6. For every borough i, calculate a one-sample z-score: zᵢ = (Sᵢ – µ) / σ.

7. Identify significant local extremes:

   • COLD spot if zᵢ < –2.576 or, failing that, zᵢ < –1.96.  
   • No label if |zᵢ| ≤ 1.96.

9. data_points_used = len(S)   # should be 32 after dropping the one missing value.

10. Print exactly two lines, nothing else:

coder_result.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------ 1. load data ------------------
crime_path = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2018.csv"
adj_path   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime_df = pd.read_csv(crime_path)           # columns: borough, crime_rate_value
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(adj_path)             # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------ 2. drop the NaN borough ------------------
nan_boroughs = crime_df[crime_df['crime_rate_value'].isna()]['borough'].tolist()
crime_df = crime_df.dropna(subset=['crime_rate_value']).reset_index(drop=True)

# make a quick lookup Series for crime rates (only non-missing)
crime_rate = crime_df.set_index('borough')['crime_rate_value']

# ------------------ 3. build undirected neighbour dict ------------------
# Collect neighbours in both directions
adj_undirected = pd.concat([
    adj_df,
    adj_df.rename(columns={'borough':'neighbor', 'neighbor':'borough'})
])

neigh_dict = {}
for row in adj_undirected.itertuples(index=False):
    b, n = row
    if (b in nan_boroughs) or (n in nan_boroughs):      # drop any link containing the NaN borough
        continue
    neigh_dict.setdefault(b, set()).add(n)

# ensure every borough appears (even isolates, though none expected)
for b in crime_rate.index:
    neigh_dict.setdefault(b, set())

# ------------------ 4. local sums (borough + its neighbours) ------------------
local_sums = {}
for b in crime_rate.index:
    local_set = {b} | neigh_dict[b]
    local_sums[b] = crime_rate.loc[list(local_set)].sum()

local_sums_series = pd.Series(local_sums)

# ------------------ 5. z-scores of the local sums ------------------
mu  = local_sums_series.mean()
sig = local_sums_series.std(ddof=1)
z_scores = (local_sums_series - mu) / sig

# ------------------ 6. identify significant HOT / COLD spots ------------------
results = []
for b, z in z_scores.items():
    label = None
    if z > 2.576:
        label = "HOT"
    elif z < -2.576:
        label = "COLD"
    elif 1.96 < z <= 2.576:
        label = "HOT"
    elif -2.576 <= z < -1.96:
        label = "COLD"
    
    if label:
        results.append(f"{b} ({label}, z-score = {z:.3f})")

# ------------------ 7. final printing ------------------
data_points_used = len(crime_rate)
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
